changes.headline: Friday rallied to six month highs into the Brent expiry, and December WCS tightened on 990 lots
changes.dek: Friday settles: WTI Dec26 $104.12 (was $102.00 Thursday), Brent Dec26 final settle $117.64 on its expiry day (was $114.88 Thursday), Brent Jan27 $113.43 (new front month); both benchmarks at their highest closes since end April; October monthly gains Brent +13.6 percent, WTI +15.2 percent. December WCS -$29.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 30) on 990 lots, was -$30.50 on 1 lot Thursday and -$31.10 on 200 lots Wednesday. ARV to TMW December spread +$6.99 (was +$7.53). Diesel crack $97.08 (was $90.42). CFTC through Oct 27: WTI net long +31,128, Brent +245,457.. WTI settled at $104.12, up $2.12, and Brent December at $117.64, up $2.76 on its expiry day, with Brent January at $113.43, up $2.63 (settles, Oct 30, Reuters, Houston; the same prices ran in the Bloomberg prices box). Both benchmarks closed at their highest levels since end April. The December to January Brent gap at expiry is $4.21 of backwardation, so Monday's front month headline steps down by $4.21 on the roll alone; it is a mechanical step, not a selloff. The Brent to WTI spread is $13.52 on the expiring December pair and $9.31 on the going forward pair (January Brent against December WTI). Post settlement, both benchmarks pared gains after the President said peace talks are taking place. In Canada, December WCS tightened to -$29.75 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 30) on 990 lots, the first volume backed tightening print of the week after Wednesday's -$31.10 traded 200 lots and Thursday's -$30.50 traded one lot. January is -$28.05. Houston December is -$22.76 on 130 lots, and the December ARV to TMW spread compressed to +$6.99 from +$7.53, so the barrels that can move are paid less to move even as Hardisty tightens. Positioning through Oct 27 (CFTC, released Oct 30): WTI managed money net long +31,128, a seventh straight weekly decline into the lower fifth of its one year range; Brent net long +245,457, a third straight build, is the crowded side.
changes.balance_read: The Canadian front is recovering on traded volume at the same time as its export spread compresses, which reads as the constraint moving rather than easing: Hardisty barrels are bid back from the widest print of the episode while the Houston premium for moving them shrinks. Flat price closed the month at six month highs with the prompt Brent backwardation at $4.21 through the expiry, and November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) takes effect with the new month, so the physical backdrop to December barrels does not loosen.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 30 to 31, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 30, 2026; CFTC Commitments of Traders, released Oct 30, 2026; validated crack history refreshed Oct 31, 2026

changes.headline: Correction: the reserve award sheets name the buyers, and the two completed sales total 40.55 million barrels
changes.dek: FY27 Sale No. 1: 16,750,000 of 17,000,000 barrels awarded to five named companies. FY26 Sale No. 4: 23,800,000 of 40,000,000 barrels awarded to six named companies (sheet dated Oct 13). Combined 40.55 million barrels. The Oct 30 edition, following the announcement release, reported that no companies were named; that was wrong. Northeast heating oil reserve: still no award document posted (positive read of the award page, Oct 31).. Checked directly on Oct 31, the Energy Department's Award Information sheets name the buyers for both completed sales. FY27 Sale No. 1 awarded 16,750,000 barrels: Trafigura 4,875,000; Gunvor USA 4,600,000; Vitol 4,150,000; Phillips 66 1,350,000; plus one additional awardee at 1,775,000. FY26 Sale No. 4 awarded 23,800,000 barrels: ExxonMobil 16,000,000; Atlantic Trading and Marketing 2,450,000; Gunvor 1,350,000; Energy Transfer 550,000; Trafigura 300,000; plus one additional awardee at 3,150,000. The combined 40.55 million barrels sit inside the 172 million barrel commitment the Oct 29 announcement completed, with more than 216 million barrels, including 44 million premium barrels, scheduled to return from early next year. The Department's newsroom carries nothing newer than the Oct 29 announcement, and no award document has been posted for the Northeast heating oil reserve exchange (bids closed Oct 27, deliveries due by Nov 13); the only Northeast reserve item posted remains an August 2025 sale notice. The correction is recorded in the Oct 31 edition: the FY26 detail was public from Oct 13 while the absence was being repeated.
changes.balance_read: The release programme is fully awarded with names attached, so the remaining reserve story is scheduling: deliveries out, and from early next year the return flow of more than 216 million barrels, 44 million of it premium barrels owed back above what was taken. That return schedule is a 2027 supply fact attached to named counterparties.
changes.publishers: US Department of Energy Award Information sheets and newsroom, checked directly Oct 31, 2026; US Department of Energy, Oct 29, 2026

changes.headline: Imperial's quarter supports the synthetic return with operator confirmed turnaround completions, and Cenovus reports Wednesday
changes.dek: Imperial Q3 (Oct 30): record net income C$2,454 million (C$5.11 a share); upstream 418,000 boe/d; Kearl 282,000 bbl/d gross (200,000 share) through third party pipeline outages including full shutdown days; Cold Lake 139,000 bbl/d with the Mahihkan turnaround completed in October; Syncrude share 70,000 bbl/d with the Coker 8-2 turnaround confirmed complete; Kearl 2026 target cut to 280,000 bbl/d gross, below the 285,000 to 295,000 guide. Cenovus did not report Oct 31; it reports Wednesday Nov 4 (company notice, Oct 28). An early version of this edition carried Saturday Cenovus results; those figures are withdrawn.. Imperial Oil's third quarter (company release and call, Oct 30) is the first fundamental check on the synthetic return verdict the tape scored on Oct 23 (SYN Dec26 settled +$5.70 on 300 lots; Friday's mark is +$5.95 on zero lots). Kearl produced 282,000 bbl/d gross (200,000 share) in a quarter hit by third party pipeline events, including a transformer failure in mid September and an 18 day outage from late August that caused a full production shutdown for multiple days. Cold Lake produced 139,000 bbl/d, and the Mahihkan turnaround was completed in October, ahead of schedule and on budget. The Syncrude share was 70,000 bbl/d, and the company confirms the Syncrude Coker 8-2 turnaround is now complete, the first operator side confirmation that the roughly 50 day coker window ended as scheduled, with interconnect imports adding about 10,000 bbl/d of share production. The Kearl 2026 target is cut to 280,000 bbl/d gross, below the original 285,000 to 295,000 range; Cold Lake and Syncrude track the low end of their 2026 ranges, with a strong fourth quarter flagged and no planned shutdowns. Downstream income was a record C$1,555 million on throughput of 381,000 bbl/d at 88 percent utilization. Cenovus Energy reports Wednesday Nov 4 (company notice, Oct 28; BOE Report calendar, Oct 30); its Lima fall turnaround carries a guided fourth quarter throughput impact of 40 to 50 kb/d. MEG Energy has no standalone report, having become a Cenovus subsidiary on Nov 13, 2025. All AESO monitored SAGD cogen units were at full maximum capability on Oct 31 with the grid at Normal.
changes.balance_read: Canadian supply keeps printing into a constrained front while the fall maintenance overhang is now operator confirmed over: the returning Joliet refinery is offset inside the quarter by the Lima turnaround's guided impact, and November's forecast maintenance takes mining and Kearl barrels offline in the same month apportionment steps up to 19 and 7 percent.
changes.publishers: Imperial Oil third quarter release, Oct 30, 2026; Cenovus Energy third quarter release, Oct 31, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Oct 30, 2026; AESO Current Supply Demand via the SAGD cogen watch, Oct 31, 2026

flags.title: Hormuz: a new projectile incident east of Aden, mine claims denied again, Ras Tanura at day four unconfirmed, and the carrier action date is Nov 1
flags.detail: UKMTO Warning 188-26 (Oct 31, 0152 UTC): a projectile impacted the water about 200 metres from a vessel about 65 nautical miles east of Aden; crew safe. That is the Gulf of Aden theatre, not the strait, and no new Hormuz warning has issued since Thursday's verified hull attachment incident (Warning 187-26). The Revolutionary Guard again claimed three tankers struck mines and US Central Command denied it again on Oct 30 in the same terms, that the claims are false and the routes remain cleared. October closes with a record 29 vessel incidents (IMO via Vortexa). Iran's president conditioned any strait closure on being attacked, in remarks carried on a single wire. The Houthi claim wave against Saudi facilities, including Ras Tanura, is at day four: no Saudi, coalition or Aramco statement addresses damage at any named oil facility, and no loading or export loss is reported. From Nov 1 the strait authority threatens legal action against all vessels of the carrier behind 47 percent of September's Hormuz VLCC transits; preliminary October loadings west of Hormuz ran about 11 Mb/d against 14.5 before the war (Vortexa via Windward). Trade the loadings, not the claim count. Trigger: A Saudi or Aramco damage statement, loading evidence of an interruption at any named facility, enforcement against a vessel of the threatened carrier on or after Nov 1, or a tier 1 flow print stepping down

flags.title: Waiver cargoes: the disclosure deadline falls Oct 31 with no reported action, and the cargo identity dispute is unresolved
flags.detail: The senator's letter demanding the first waiver tanker's owner recall the vessel and disclose the seller, buyer, charterer, insurer and terminal operator reaches its deadline on Oct 31. As of this edition's checks there is no reported compliance, recall, US delivery or port state action on any waiver vessel. The cargo identity question stands unresolved on the public record: most reporting describes diesel, while a tanker tracking service assesses the two later St. Petersburg departures carry UAN fertilizer, which is not sanctioned and is authorised for US import. No US delivery of any waiver cargo has been confirmed. Russia's November diesel quota exports are 2 million tonnes and its refinery runs stand at 4.0 Mb/d on the last reported week. Trigger: A disclosure filing or recall by the vessel's owner, a confirmed US delivery of a waiver cargo, a port state action, or a cargo manifest resolving the diesel versus fertilizer question

flags.title: December apportionment: the nowcast is persistence at 19 and 7, no judgment call is registered, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) takes effect with the new month. December's outlook opens at persistence on those levels. The evidence pack for a December call now includes Friday's traded December tightening (990 lots at -$29.75), the export spread's compression through $7, Imperial's reported volumes, and November's forecast maintenance overlap at the mining complex and Kearl. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; an unregistered call after that date is a lost data point for the prediction record. Trigger: Registration of a December judgment call, the Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop
